g11-history-uh2-t1.overview: Ancient Civilizations of Africa sits inside Major Spots of Ancient World Civilizations up to c.500 A.D. Ancient civilizations shape Unit 2 of Grade 11 History, framed by the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the civilizations of Africa in Egypt and Kush-Meroe along the Nile. Then the Asian civilizations of Mesopotamia, India, and China. Next, ancient Greece and Rome in Europe. Also the Maya, Aztec, and Inca of Latin America. Finally, the rise and spread of Christianity across the Roman world. Students will also learn how these ancient civilizations apply to real-life situations today, from writing and law to calendars and medicine.
objectives: Explain how each major civilization arose and then declined.
Compare the ancient civilizations of Africa, Asia, Europe, and Latin America.
Describe the achievements of Egypt, Mesopotamia, Greece, Rome, and the Americas.
Analyse the role of rivers and trade in early state formation.
Discuss how Christianity reshaped belief in the Roman world.
g11-history-uh2-t1.simple:
Ancient Civilizations of Africa in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the ancient civilizations of Africa in Egypt, the gift of the Nile, with pharaohs, pyramids, and writing.
  • Then the kingdom of Kush-Meroe, its iron working, trade, and pyramids along the Nile.
g11-history-uh2-t1.detailed:
Ancient Civilizations of Africa — the essentials. First, the ancient civilizations of Africa in Egypt, the gift of the Nile, with pharaohs, pyramids, and writing. Then the kingdom of Kush-Meroe, its iron working, trade, and pyramids along the Nile.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain how each major civilization arose and then declined.
  • Compare the ancient civilizations of Africa, Asia, Europe, and Latin America.
  • Describe the achievements of Egypt, Mesopotamia, Greece, Rome, and the Americas.
  • Analyse the role of rivers and trade in early state formation.
  • Discuss how Christianity reshaped belief in the Roman world.
